chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Hammad ibn Abi al-Hakam, from his father, from Hammad ibn Isa, from Hariz, from Zurara, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said:
By Allah, indeed disbelief (Kufr) is earlier than polytheism (Shirk), and more foul and greater.
He said, then he mentioned the disbelief of Iblis when Allah said to him, 'Prostrate to Adam,' but he refused to prostrate.
So disbelief is greater than polytheism.
So whoever chooses against Allah, Mighty and Majestic, and refuses obedience and persists in major sins, then he is a disbeliever (Kafir).
And whoever establishes a religion other than the religion of the believers, then he is a polytheist (Mushrik).
ai.seo_question: What is the difference between Kufr and Shirk according to Imam al-Baqir?
ai.summary: Imam al-Baqir (peace be upon him) establishes a hierarchical distinction where Kufr (disbelief) is fundamentally more severe than Shirk (polytheism), using Iblis's initial refusal to obey Allah's command as the archetype of Kufr. He clarifies that while a Mushrik adopts a divergent religious system, a Kafir is defined by the conscious choice to defy Allah and persist in major sins, highlighting the primacy of willful rejection over ritual deviation.

en.hubeali:
Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Hammad Bin Isa, from Hareyz, from Zurara, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Ja’far<sup>asws</sup> having said:
‘By Allahazwj! The disbelief (Kufr) occurred earlier than the association (Shirk) and is worse and more grievous’.

He (the narrator) said, ‘Then he<sup style="font-weight: normal">asws</sup> mentioned: ‘Iblees<sup style="font-weight: normal">la</sup> disbelieved where Allah<sup style="font-weight: normal">azwj</sup> Told him<sup style="font-weight: normal">la</sup> to prostrate to Adam<sup style="font-weight: normal">as</sup>, but he<sup style="font-weight: normal">la</sup> refused to prostrate.
Hence, the disbelief (Kufr) is more grievous than the association (Shirk).
So the one who chooses against Allahazwj Mighty and Majestic and refuses the obedience and stands upon the major sins, so he is a Unbeliver (Kafir);
and the one who establishes a religion other than the Religion of the Momineenasws, so he is a Polytheist (Mushrik)’.
en.sarwar: 2. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father from Hammad ibn ‘Isa from Hariz from Zurara from abu Ja’far (a.s.) who has said the following: “
By Allah, disbelief is before paganism and it is greater in filth.
The narrator has said that the Imam then mentioned the disbelief of Satan when Allah told him to bow down before Adam and refused to prostrate,
that disbelief is greater than considering things partners of Allah.
Whoever chooses something instead of Allah, the Most Majestic, the Most Holy, refuses to obey and commits major sins is an unbeliever.
One who establishes a religion other than the religion of the believers has considered things as partners of Allah.”
